passage: Abstract: "record-wise CV often massively overestimates the prediction accuracy of the algorithms"; "the subject-wise method mirrors the clinically relevant use-case scenario of diagnosis in newly recruited subjects".
faulty: Record-wise 10-fold cross-validation: the 900 windows (30 subjects x 30 windows) are assigned to folds uniformly at random; a random forest (50 trees) classifies walking from the 40 features; the error rate pooled over folds is the statistic. Claim holds when error <= 0.10.
fixed: Subject-wise 10-fold cross-validation: all windows of a subject are in the same fold (3 subjects per fold); same forest and statistic.
estimand: Faulty: error on windows whose subject also appears in the fitting data. Fixed: error on windows of subjects never used in fitting.
model_family: Random forest, 50 trees: the source's classifier (activity recognition, tuned on out-of-bag error; I fix the settings).
sizes_note: Source sizes: 30 subjects, 10,299 records (about 343 per subject), 561 features, 6 activities (full text via Europe PMC). I use 30 subjects x 30 windows x 40 features = 36k values and a binary label because 30 x 343 x 561 exceeds 2 000 000 values and a check on it would exceed about 30 minutes (rough estimate). Source on dependence: the gap between record-wise and subject-wise error is largest with few subjects (subject-wise 27% at 2 subjects falling to 9% at 30, record-wise about 2% throughout); records per subject and features were not varied.
exploited_structure: Repeated records of one subject: windows from the same subject are far more alike than windows from different subjects.

structure_statistic.code:
def stat(d):
    x = np.asarray(d["signal_features"], dtype=float)
    s, m, v = x.shape
    site_mean = x.mean(axis=1)
    grand = x.mean(axis=(0, 1))
    msb = m * ((site_mean - grand) ** 2).sum(axis=0) / (s - 1)
    msw = ((x - site_mean[:, None, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=(0, 1)) / (s * (m - 1))
    den = msb + (m - 1) * msw
    ok = den > 0
    if not np.any(ok):
        return 0.0
    icc = (msb - msw)[ok] / den[ok]
    return float(np.mean(icc))
structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the simulation's cross-subject variability b is a parameter whose values I did not read; 0.3 is a proposed between-subject share of feature variance

notes: Six activities reduced to a bool (walking) because binary labels are bool and group codes may not be integers. The ICC is of the features, not of the labels, so a claim-false world that replaces the label keeps it.
